questions.q: Gel, BIAB or acrylic: which should I have?
questions.a: Gel for colour on healthy nails, BIAB to strengthen weak or bitten nails while they grow, acrylic for length. Send a photo and we'll tell you.
No. Book removal as its own thirty minutes. We'll remove gel or BIAB from another salon too.

questions.q: Can I bring my own polish?
questions.a: We use our own gels so we can stand behind the finish. Regular polish you bring is fine for a shape and polish.

questions.q: Are your gels HEMA-free and vegan?
questions.a: Our house gels are vegan and cruelty-free. We keep a HEMA-free range; ask when you book if you need it.

questions.q: Is BIAB bad for my nails?
questions.a: Not when it's filed back and infilled rather than soaked off each time. Picking or peeling it off is what thins nails.

questions.q: How often do I need an infill?
questions.a: Every three to four weeks. Regrowth shows sooner on dark shades.
Gel or BIAB that chips or lifts within seven days is fixed free. Send us a photo first.

questions.q: Can I have gel while pregnant? Are the lamps safe?
questions.a: Many people do; it's your choice. Tell us when you book, and ask your midwife if you're unsure.

questions.q: Can I bring a friend, or my baby?
questions.a: Yes. There's room on the sofa by the window.
Yes, the counter is on the ground floor. The toilet is downstairs.

pages.title: Aftercare and infills
pages.description: How to look after gel and BIAB between visits at Verrall, Marylebone.
pages.intro: Two minutes a day keeps a set for its full three or four weeks.

blocks.heading: The first day
blocks.body: Gel and BIAB are fully set when you leave. Keep hot baths and saunas for the next day; heat can soften the top coat while it settles.

blocks.heading: Every day
blocks.body:
Cuticle oil morning and night. Gloves for washing up and cleaning. Use the pads of your fingers, not your nails, to open things.

If an edge lifts, don't pick it: picking takes a layer of your own nail with it.

blocks.heading: Infills
blocks.body: BIAB every three to four weeks. Regrowth shows sooner on dark shades, so a shorter gap suits Claret and Onyx.
